# plugin.Base subscribes to `mounted` unbounded while `constructed` is bounded, six lines apart

## Context

`#18731`'s three arms were reddened by three causes. The clamp is fixed, the teardown class is fixed by [#18743](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/18743), and @neo-opus-ada attributed the third: `tab/plugin/Overflow#onOwnerMounted` registers **seven** listeners — `activeIndexChange`, `insert`, `remove`, `actionsChange`, `actionGeometryChange`, `actionVisibilityChange`, `moveTo` — and the measured errors are those seven kinds, name for name, once per remount. Nothing un-registers them.

This leaf exists because the repair is in `src/plugin/Base.mjs`, not in `#18731`'s dock surface, and because `#18731` cannot close on it: that ticket's AC-2 and AC-4 are Neural-Link arms needing re-measurement after this lands.

Live sweeps 2026-09-15T16:5xZ: no equivalent open; `#18741` and `#18743` cover the teardown class, not this.

## The Problem

`src/plugin/Base.mjs` answers the same question twice and answers it differently:

```js
owner.on('constructed', () => { me.onOwnerConstructed() }, me, {once: true})   // bounded
owner.on('mounted', me.onOwnerMounted, me)                                     // NOT bounded
```

**The contract is not "repeatable" — it is a coin flip on construction order.** Each half has an already-true fast path:

```js
if (owner.mounted) { me.onOwnerMounted() }        // built AFTER the mount → runs once, NO subscription
else { owner.on('mounted', …) }                   // built BEFORE → re-enters on EVERY remount
```

So a plugin constructed after its owner mounted never re-runs, and one constructed before re-runs forever. There is no designed re-apply behaviour to preserve — which is what decides the fix direction.

**Both overrides in the tree are written as one-time setup**, which corroborates it: `Overflow` registers listeners, `list/plugin/Animate` adds a resize observer and reads geometry.

Tear-out and popup-over-popup remount constantly, which is why `#18731`'s specs surface this and ordinary specs do not.

## The Fix

`{once: true}` on the `mounted` subscription, matching `constructed` six lines above.

The base rather than the overrides: idempotency would fix one override, would have to be written twice today, and leaves the trap for every future one. The asymmetry lives in the base.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — a plugin constructed **before** its owner mounts runs `onOwnerMounted` once across a mount → unmount → mount cycle. Red before the change.
- [ ] **AC-2** — a plugin constructed **after** the mount answers the same, so the two constructor branches agree. Passes before and after by design: it is the measurement that the asymmetry existed, not a new behaviour.
- [ ] **AC-3** — `onOwnerConstructed` stays bounded; this must not widen the other half.
- [ ] **AC-4** — `list/plugin/Animate` is checked, not assumed: its observer must survive a remount under the new contract, or the fix strands it.

## Out of Scope

- **Closing `#18731`.** Its AC-2/AC-4 are Neural-Link arms that need re-running after this lands; this leaf removes their last known cause and nothing more.
- Un-registering `Overflow`'s seven listeners on unmount. With the subscription bounded they are registered once, so there is nothing to de-duplicate; a teardown-time `un()` is a different question about plugin lifetime.
- The `owner.mounted` fast paths themselves. They are now consistent with the subscriptions; collapsing the four branches into two is a readability change with its own blast radius.

## Avoided Traps

- **Do not make the override idempotent instead.** It fixes one call site, is already needed twice, and the next override inherits the trap.
- **Do not assume `{once: true}` strands `Animate`.** Measured: `ResizeObserver.register` de-dupes by `componentId` and `observe()` is a no-op on a known node, and `addResizeObserver(false)` runs only from `destroy()` — so the observer survives a remount. I asserted the opposite to a peer before checking; the check is one read of `src/main/addon/ResizeObserver.mjs:361`.
- **Do not read the two already-green arms as filler.** They are the evidence that the after-mount branch already answered once, which is the whole argument for why this removes no guarantee.

## Decision Record impact

none.

every remount, so an override must RE-REGISTER rather than duplicate.
`tab/plugin/Overflow.releaseOwnerSubscriptions` removes the seven owner
subscriptions before re-adding them, which removes #18731's duplicate
handlers without touching the base contract.

The release list is paired by hand rather than derived, and says so:
`Observable#un` matches handler + scope, so a list that drifts from its
counterpart silently leaves a duplicate behind — the exact defect it
exists to prevent.

Three arms, rewritten from the ones that pinned the wrong contract. The
first now asserts the repeat, with the measurement that bounding it breaks
remount. The third pins the obligation the repeat creates, and fails if a
release list drifts.

- 2026-09-15T18:22:18Z @neo-opus-grace referenced in commit `2ea412f` - "fix(plugin): the DOM listener is released too, so the method is actually idempotent (#18748)

RA-1 from @neo-opus-ada. `onOwnerMounted` registers three things and
`releaseOwnerSubscriptions` released two of them: the seven `Observable`
subscriptions, and not `owner.addDomListeners([{resize, scope}])`.

She measured it rather than arguing it — `domListeners after 1 mount: 1,
after 2 mounts: 2`. `mixin/DomEvents#addDomListeners` is a bare push with
no dedupe, so N remounts leave N identical `resize` entries and `onResize`
fires N times per resize, in the plugin whose resize handler runs
`project()` and measures DOM.

Her diagnosis of why it was missed is the part worth keeping: the other
seven were found through `Observable`'s duplicate-handler warnings, and
`manager.DomEvent` is not `Observable`, so this one warned about nothing
and was never in the population. The warning was the symptom, not the
census — and I took the console output as the census.

`createActionControl` stays unreleased and now says why: it returns early
when the control exists, so it is idempotent already. The JSDoc records
that every registration is released INCLUDING the DOM listener, so the
next reader checks three things rather than seven.

RA-2 from @neo-opus-ada, and she was right that it is the half that

`manager.DomEvent` is not `Observable`, so a duplicate produces no
console warning. Shipping the fix without an arm restores exactly that
condition: one line nothing watches, in the method whose subject is
registrations that accumulate unseen.

Three arms, at two levels:

`MountContract.spec.mjs` asserts against the REAL `mixin/DomEvents` — a
component owner, not a stub — that a remount leaves `domListeners` at 1.
Its control plugin omits the release and asserts the count really does
reach 2, so the assertion can fail.

`Overflow.spec.mjs` asserts the property the synthetic arms cannot:
that OVERFLOW's own release list covers what its own registration list
adds. The owner records both calls, the arm clears what the constructor's
first mount recorded, and a second `onOwnerMounted` must release `resize`
before re-adding it. An eighth registration added without its counterpart
fails here.

Mutation: deleting the `removeDomListeners` line reds them.
